content: How science and engineering teams can put AI to work Date & time 14 th Oct 2026 · 4:30pm BST / 11:30am ET / 8:30am PT Register now Only 36% of practitioners use AI in core engineering work. Interest in AI runs high across chemistry, hardware, and engineering teams, but few have found where it holds up in core design and delivery work. This session covers examples of where AI is accelerating science and engineering today: evaluating new cooling fluids from molecule screening through to process performance, sizing liquid-cooling hardware from system requirements, and taking a data center client spec through concept design to submittal documents. Hear directly from the Orbital Industries team on where AI has earned trust in their own projects. Agenda at a glance Open A quick introduction to Orbital Industries, the projects we work on, and how we've built the expertise behind them. Materials, hardware, and deployment engineering Matt (PhD), Graham (PhD), and Jaden (P.Eng.) share examples, covering what's changed in their day-to-day workflows and where AI has earned trust. Learn how AI is impacting each domain, drawn from real projects in materials, hardware, and deployment engineering. Q&A follows. See how we run CurieOS in-house Demo of how we use CurieOS day-to-day, Orbital Industries' AI operating system for science and engineering. Speaker lineup Jonathan Godwin Co-Founder & CEO Orbital Industries Matthew Kapelewski, PhD Director of Chemistry Orbital Industries Graham Wenz, PhD Director of Engineering Orbital Industries Jaden Weaver, P.Eng. Senior Mechanical Engineer Orbital Industries Ruxy Chitac, PhD Technical Product Manager Orbital Industries Save your seat Register to hear where AI works in different engineering domains today, and where it doesn't, straight from real engineering projects and the experts inside Orbital Industries.
